video_title: Fred VanVleet is EXACTLY What the Rockets Were Missing | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Houston Rockets' top-10 offensive and defensive efficiency ratings
quotes.excerpt: If you're top 10 in both categories, you are by definition a championship contender.
quotes.quote: They are second in the NBA in offensive rating. They are ninth in the NBA in defensive rating. If you're top 10 in both categories, you are by definition a championship contender.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Houston Rockets' efficient play and physical depth
quotes.excerpt: They're getting efficient, quality shots and they're moving the ball around as well.
quotes.quote: They're getting down, they're not rushing things, but they're getting efficient, quality shots and they're moving the ball around as well. I think this is a sign of a good team, especially early on. But the most important thing is their depth and their size and physicality. They're just big as hell. They're able to get into people, they have a lot of experience. Marcus Smart has missed four games, Steven Adams has missed a couple games, but you're going on the bench and you're pulling out Bojan Bogdanovic, that's your eighth or ninth man. There are some elite players here.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Fred VanVleet's steady leadership impact on the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Fred VanVleet is a steady, reliable guy out there. He's going to give you 30-ish minutes.
quotes.quote: I was preaching that Fred VanVleet is going to matter. Forget the numbers. Last couple of years he has not been a high-efficiency guy. He's still not a high-efficiency guy, but he is a steady, reliable guy out there. He's going to give you 30-ish minutes per game and be able to initiate the offense. And him being there, I've heard Kevin Durant talk about this, it allows everybody else to slot back into their usual positions. Alperen Sengun doesn't need to be the point guard on this team. Reed Sheppard doesn't need to be the starting point guard on this team. Kevin Durant doesn't need to have the ball in his hands initiating some of the offense. It just allows everybody to be themselves.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Reed Sheppard's potential for improved three-point shooting
quotes.excerpt: Reed Sheppard is too good a shooter to shoot 28% from three.
quotes.quote: Reed Sheppard is shooting like 28% from three. He's shooting like eight of them per game, 28.1% from three. That number is going to go way up. Reed Sheppard is too good a shooter to shoot 28% from three. If he gets into the mid to high 30s, that offense, that already potent offense, is going to be really, really good.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Rockets' potential for roster upgrades before the trade deadline
quotes.excerpt: Rafael Stone has done an excellent job of doing the deals that he has.
quotes.quote: Rafael Stone has done an excellent job of doing the deals that he has, most notably the Kevin Durant deal, but not getting rid of all his assets. He's still got some draft picks he can deal. He's still got some very interesting young players that might be attractive to teams. You got Jabari Smith, who's having a heck of a start to the season. You got Reed Sheppard, who is a really good player, former third overall draft pick. We keep hearing the name Kyrie Irving that's out there and I think Kyrie will be out there. Could you imagine Kyrie Irving with this team?

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of adding a superstar like Kyrie Irving to Houston
quotes.excerpt: You add Kyrie, you obviously a level that takes it to superstar-dom championship contender.
quotes.quote: You add Kyrie, you obviously a level that takes it to superstar-dom championship contender, media, and everything else. What do you think that does to the overall camaraderie? Do you go from like a team that's in depth, that has 10 hard-nosed blue-collar guys, or does it switch over where Kyrie is going to play 32 minutes and now we're kind of going to a finesse brand of basketball that sometimes I feel this all might dial back because Fred VanVleet, his background is tough, Wichita State, getting out the mud is gritty.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving's high trade value and Dallas's potential interest
quotes.excerpt: I think he's going to be the most in-demand player at the trade deadline.
quotes.quote: I think Kyrie is a separate topic. I think he's going to be the most in-demand player at the trade deadline because he's not on the Mavericks' timeline. I think Detroit is another team that will be salivating over getting Kyrie Irving. They're off to a great start. I think the Mavericks have a chance to get some real assets back in return for a player that's been good for them.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Teams attempting to replicate the LeBron-Kyrie championship formula
quotes.excerpt: They try to find a LeBron build and just throw Kyrie with them.
quotes.quote: You ever notice they always just they try to find a LeBron build and just throw Kyrie with them and they're like, yo, you might make the championship. Because of LeBron, Kyrie, then they threw Luka, Kyrie together and it's like, you know, Kevin Durant is one of those people that only people that done what only people that done with Kevin Durant is done is Kyrie and LeBron. And you see that big 6-7, 6-8 do-it-all point four and then you just see a killer scorer right next to him.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Dallas Mavericks' future need for a Kyrie Irving replacement
quotes.excerpt: Five years from now, Dallas is going to be looking for the next Kyrie Irving.
quotes.quote: Five years from now, Dallas is going to be looking for the next Kyrie Irving, someone that can play opposite Luka Doncic once they hopefully ascend to a different level. I watch the Pistons some, when Jalen Duren is your secondary scorer, that's fine for some regular season games, but in the playoffs you're going to get beat. You put Kyrie next to Luka, who, you put Kyrie next to Kevin Durant, who.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's decision-making and playmaking in clutch moments
quotes.excerpt: They put the ball in Luka's hands. Luka can make some plays, man.
quotes.quote: I watched the Dallas-Miami game the other night. Down the stretch, usually when Kyrie would have the ball to kind of do Kyrie things, they put the ball in Luka's hands. Luka can make some plays, man. Luka was making some plays. I was skeptical, but Luka is and he could have had 40 something. He literally was getting his guys and that's a bad boy, bruh. When I saw that, I said, man, he is better than Giannis. And Giannis is an old-school attack mode and Luka was on some chill, I know how to win type. Did you feel that? He was almost like, I know how to win.
